value.name: live pij-rs daemon
value.note: 127.0.0.1:7461, bearer from ~/.pij-rs/daemon.key. Every criterion below is measured against the RUNNING daemon; a fixture cannot prove a reader tracks a fleet.

value.name: process table
value.note: ps is the only honest witness that no child process is being spawned per tick — the defect this plan exists to remove.

value.criterion: With PIJ_SOURCE=rs, next-server spawns no pij child process.
value.proof: RUN: start dev with PIJ_SOURCE=rs, wait 60s, then `ps -Ao command | grep -c '[c]li.ts list --json'` -> must print 0.
value.note: The pre-state is measured and on record: 2 in flight continuously, ~95% of a core, top two consumers on the machine.

value.criterion: An RsPijRecords read of a live seat equals a direct /v1/seats read of the same id at the same moment.
value.proof: RUN: `node scripts/verify-rs-reader.mjs --seat <live-id>` — reads both, diffs every mapped field, exits non-zero on mismatch.
value.note: Deliberately NOT 'matches the legacy reader': the two daemons disagree about which seat a process IS (1 same id, 3 renamed, 24 absent across 28 live seats), and legacy is being retired. Comparing against a dying, inconsistent comparator would prove nothing.

value.criterion: A seat that appears in the fleet appears in the reader within 2s.
value.proof: RUN: `pij-rs adopt` a scratch pane; assert the new id is visible through the reader within 2s.

value.criterion: NEGATIVE — the reader mirrors /v1/seats faithfully, INCLUDING tombstones once pij-rs sets them.
value.proof: RUN: adopt a scratch pane, confirm it reaches the reader, kill it, then assert the reader's row for that id matches a direct /v1/seats read at the same moment — including tombstoned_at, whatever its value. The reader must never disagree with the daemon in either direction.
value.note: RE-SPECIFIED 2026-09-03, and the original is kept here because the reason matters more than the row. It read 'a closed seat disappears from the reader within 2s'. That is UNMEETABLE: pij-rs does not reap or tombstone a dead seat. Measured — scratch seat pij-semantic-pennyroyal, pane killed, pid confirmed dead by ps, still listed untombstoned as state:'idle' 175s later. Census of the whole roster: 716 of 744 untombstoned paned seats (96%) point at panes that do not exist, and all 716 report 'idle'. Independently reproduced by pij-binding-magpie with a different script, same numbers to the row. An rs row carries no liveness key, so a corpse and a quiet live seat are BYTE-IDENTICAL. This is NOT a defect in the reader: bp-0002 compared 838 seats with zero field mismatches. The criterion was measuring pij-rs's behaviour, not ours. It is re-specified rather than dropped because dropping it would have hidden precisely this finding. KNOWN LIMITATION, tracked as oq-0004: until pij-rs reaps, a chainglass rail on rs shows dead seats as healthy idle ones. chainglass will NOT derive liveness from pid+proc_start — that re-implements pij's contract outside pij and would silently diverge the first time their definition of dead changes. Roadmap question routed to Jordan. METHOD GAP CLOSED BY pij-capitalist-boa, recorded because my control could not have caught it: `tmux list-panes -a` enumerates only the tmux server on the socket you are attached to, so a seat living in a DIFFERENT server (-L name, or another TMUX_TMPDIR) would be invisible and counted dead. My 28-alive control proves the matcher resolves panes in the server it can reach and says nothing about one it cannot. boa measured it instead of caveating it: /tmp/tmux-501 holds 5967 socket entries, but exactly TWO live servers (default, 60 panes; simple-demo, 1 non-pij pane) — 61 live panes total, so exposure is one pane in another project and the 716 stands. boa's incidental finding is the better one: 5967 socket files against 2 live servers is the SAME disease as the seat registry — dead things nothing reaps, and a listing that cannot tell them from live ones. That is an independent instance of this root cause on the same machine, which argues a missing reaper is a habit here rather than one gap in rs. Third symptom, also boa's: a send to a corpse fails with 'pane_in_mode ... expected 0 or 1 — update pij-tmux', which names a tmux capability problem and sends the reader off to upgrade a package. So the gap does not only render wrong, it CORRUPTS THE DIAGNOSTIC PATH. Three symptoms, one root: renders healthy, retries hundreds of times, errors misleadingly.

value.criterion: The reader survives a daemon restart on its own, resuming from its cursor.
value.proof: RUN: restart the rs daemon under a running chainglass; assert the event stream resumes from the last cursor with no chainglass restart and no gap in sequence.

value.criterion: A rotated daemon.key causes exactly one 401-triggered re-read, then success.
value.proof: RUN: against a scratch PIJ_RS_STATE_DIR, rotate daemon.key mid-session; assert one re-read and one successful retry, and that a second failure does NOT loop.
value.note: Exercised against the real daemon with a scratch key file, not mocked — magpie's instruction. A mocked 401 proves the branch exists, not that the daemon accepts what we re-read.

value.criterion: Fields pij-rs does not carry render as explicitly unavailable, never blank.
value.proof: EXTEND->RUN: unit-assert watchdog/bindHealth/degraded map to an explicit unavailable marker; `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/pij/`.
value.note: Blank is a defect, not a cosmetic gap: an empty watchdog cell reads as 'your watchdog is off', which is false in the dangerous direction. This repo has already shipped one bug of exactly that shape (65f524ea9).

value.criterion: PIJ_SOURCE unset or =legacy leaves existing behaviour unchanged.
value.proof: RUN: `just fft` green with PIJ_SOURCE unset.
value.note: The flip is out of scope; default must not move.
